```{python}
#| echo: false
import html as html_lib
import io
import re

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px
from google.cloud import bigquery
from IPython.display import Image, Markdown
from wordcloud import STOPWORDS, WordCloud

PROJECT = "portfolio-hub-464520"
DATASET = "dbt_prod"

client = bigquery.Client(project=PROJECT)


def bq(sql, job_config=None):
    return client.query(sql, job_config=job_config).to_dataframe()


# Fixed-order categorical palette (colorblind-validated) — never cycled or
# reassigned when the underlying set of topics changes.
CATEGORICAL = ["#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100", "#e87ba4", "#008300"]
# Single-hue sequential ramp for magnitude-only (ranked) bars.
SEQUENTIAL_BLUE = ["#cde2fb", "#9ec5f4", "#6da7ec", "#3987e5", "#256abf", "#184f95", "#0d366b"]


def finalize(fig, *, left=60, bottom=50, legend_bottom=False):
    """Give every chart fixed margins and turn off automargin.

    Quarto dashboard cards resize the plot container while the page settles
    (fonts, flex layout). Plotly's automargin recalculates on each resize and
    can append new axis tick groups instead of replacing the old ones, which
    shows up as ghosted/duplicated axis labels. Fixed margins avoid that.
    """
    fig.update_xaxes(automargin=False)
    fig.update_yaxes(automargin=False)
    fig.update_layout(margin=dict(l=left, r=20, t=10, b=bottom))
    if legend_bottom:
        fig.update_layout(
            legend=dict(orientation="h", yanchor="top", y=-0.3, xanchor="left", x=0, entrywidth=150)
        )
    return fig


# Global Voices flattens region + country + topic + format + language into a
# single `categories` array per article (see gv_taxonomy seed / int_article_tags
# model). mart_tag_totals / mart_tag_daily carry a `category_type` column so we
# can slice each dimension separately instead of treating it as one bag of tags.

daily_df = bq(f"""
    select article_date, article_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_articles_daily`
    order by article_date
""")

topics_df = bq(f"""
    select tag, mention_count, last_mentioned
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'topic'
    order by mention_count desc
""")

regions_df = bq(f"""
    select tag as region_name, mention_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'region'
    order by mention_count desc
""")

countries_df = bq(f"""
    select tag as country, region, mention_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'country'
    order by mention_count desc
    limit 15
""")

top_topics = topics_df.head(6)["tag"].tolist()
topic_color_map = dict(zip(top_topics, CATEGORICAL[: len(top_topics)]))

topic_trend_df = bq(
    f"""
    select article_date, category_name, article_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_daily`
    where category_type = 'topic' and category_name in unnest(@top_topics)
    order by article_date
    """,
    job_config=bigquery.QueryJobConfig(
        query_parameters=[bigquery.ArrayQueryParameter("top_topics", "STRING", top_topics)]
    ),
)

author_df = bq(f"""
    select author, count(distinct guid) as article_count
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.stg_articles`
    where author is not null and trim(author) != ''
    group by author
    order by article_count desc
    limit 10
""")

latest_df = bq(f"""
    select
        pub_date,
        title,
        author,
        array_to_string(tags, ', ') as topics,
        link
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.stg_articles`
    order by pub_date desc
    limit 15
""")


def strip_html(raw):
    """Drop tags/entities from content_html, leaving plain running text."""
    return html_lib.unescape(re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", raw or ""))


# Site-wide boilerplate that would otherwise dominate the cloud: every
# article repeats an "Originally published on Global Voices" byline and
# photo-credit line verbatim, regardless of the story's actual content.
GV_STOPWORDS = STOPWORDS.union(
    {
        "global", "voices", "globalvoices", "originally", "published",
        "photo", "photos", "courtesy", "permission", "image", "images", "used",
        "read", "story", "said", "also", "one", "two", "will", "new",
        "including", "according", "told", "still", "even", "much", "made",
        "way", "years", "year", "first", "since", "like", "people", "may",
        "many", "us", "day", "days", "now", "say", "across", "without",
        "part", "hour", "hours", "month", "months", "three", "use", "used",
        "official", "public", "national", "local", "international", "around",
        "final", "become", "remain", "percent", "left", "right",
        "january", "february", "march", "april", "june", "july", "august",
        "september", "october", "november", "december",
    }
)

text_df = bq(f"""
    select title, description, content_html
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.stg_articles`
""")

full_text = " ".join(
    " ".join(filter(None, [row["title"], row["description"], strip_html(row["content_html"])]))
    for _, row in text_df.iterrows()
)

word_cloud = WordCloud(
    width=900,
    height=450,
    background_color=None,
    mode="RGBA",
    stopwords=GV_STOPWORDS,
    collocations=False,
    min_word_length=3,
    max_words=80,
    prefer_horizontal=0.9,
    random_state=42,
)
word_freqs = word_cloud.process_text(full_text)
word_cloud = word_cloud.generate_from_frequencies(word_freqs)

# Recolor with our single-hue sequential ramp (bigger word = more mentions =
# darker blue) instead of wordcloud's default random-hue palette.
_sizes = [size for _, size, _, _, _ in word_cloud.layout_]
_lo, _hi = min(_sizes), max(_sizes)


def _blue_by_size(word, font_size, position, orientation, random_state=None, **kwargs):
    t = 0.5 if _hi == _lo else (font_size - _lo) / (_hi - _lo)
    return SEQUENTIAL_BLUE[round(t * (len(SEQUENTIAL_BLUE) - 1))]


word_cloud = word_cloud.recolor(color_func=_blue_by_size, random_state=42)

top_words_df = pd.DataFrame(
    sorted(word_freqs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:15], columns=["word", "mentions"]
)

total_articles = int(daily_df["article_count"].sum())
days_covered = daily_df["article_date"].nunique()
topics_covered = topics_df.shape[0]
countries_covered = bq(f"""
    select count(*) as n
    from `{PROJECT}.{DATASET}.mart_tag_totals`
    where category_type = 'country'
""")["n"].iloc[0]
top_topic = topics_df.iloc[0]["tag"]
```

## Row {height="280px"}

```{python}
#| title: Daily Article Volume

fig = px.area(
    daily_df,
    x="article_date",
    y="article_count",
    labels={"article_date": "Date", "article_count": "Articles"},
    color_discrete_sequence=[CATEGORICAL[0]],
    template="plotly_white",
)
fig = fig.update_traces(line_width=2, hovertemplate="%{x|%b %d, %Y}<br>%{y} articles<extra></extra>")
fig = fig.update_yaxes(dtick=1, rangemode="tozero")
finalize(fig, left=40, bottom=40)
```

## Row {height="480px"}

```{python}
#| title: Top 15 Topics (All Time)

top15 = topics_df.head(15).sort_values("mention_count")
fig = px.bar(
    top15,
    x="mention_count",
    y="tag",
    orientation="h",
    color="mention_count",
    color_continuous_scale=SEQUENTIAL_BLUE,
    labels={"tag": "", "mention_count": "Mentions"},
    template="plotly_white",
)
fig = fig.update_layout(coloraxis_showscale=False)
finalize(fig, left=170, bottom=40)
```

```{python}
#| title: Topic Trends Over Time (Top 6)

fig = px.area(
    topic_trend_df,
    x="article_date",
    y="article_count",
    color="category_name",
    color_discrete_map=topic_color_map,
    category_orders={"category_name": top_topics},
    labels={"article_date": "Date", "article_count": "Articles", "category_name": "Topic"},
    template="plotly_white",
)
fig = fig.update_layout(legend_title_text="")
finalize(fig, left=40, bottom=110, legend_bottom=True)
```

```{python}
#| title: Latest Headlines

rows = ["| Date | Title | Author | Topics |", "|---|---|---|---|"]
for _, row in latest_df.iterrows():
    date_str = row["pub_date"].strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    title_link = f"[{row['title']}]({row['link']})"
    author = row["author"] or "—"
    rows.append(f"| {date_str} | {title_link} | {author} | {row['topics']} |")

Markdown("\n".join(rows))
```
